column3: Near-verbatim knowledge of what lies before and behind them, joined to creatures' inability to encompass divine knowledge.
States that intercession is effective only by the Merciful's permission and acceptance of speech.
Divine knowledge accompanying favor is too general to clarify the focus's intercession or fear.
Near-verbatim knowledge of what lies before and behind them, with all matters returning to God.
The non-playful creation premise supports the surrounding sovereignty argument but not the focus's three claims directly.
Knowledge of parables by the learned does not materially explain divine knowledge, intercession, or fear here.
Pairs the accepted messenger with watchfulness before and behind, echoing both acceptance and comprehensive surrounding scope.
The immediate context identifies heavenly beings as God's own, tireless servants free of pride.
Uses what is before and behind as the field of warning that should produce mercy-seeking caution.

The immediate heavenly servants continuously glorify without weariness, expanding their obedient posture.

Explicitly restricts intercession and links it to testimony to truth and knowledge.

Deferred knowledge after heedless enjoyment is a distant temporal contrast to the knowledge asserted in the focus.
God knows every soul's acquisition, reinforcing that no hidden human course escapes divine knowledge.
The nearby argument for one divine ruler grounds why no servant can exercise independent authority.
Messengers coming before and behind establish a broad warning field, though the directional wording is not divine knowledge.
Explicitly says intercession benefits only one for whom God has granted permission.
The creation sign advances the surah's sovereignty case but does not add to the focus's intercession or fear.
Contrasts limited human knowledge with the Lord's fuller knowledge of the misguided and guided.
Rejects claimed intercessors and exposes the incoherence of attributing to God what is not within the claim.
A prophet's request for decisive separation is not a substantive parallel to the focus.
Human developmental stages and diminished knowledge give only a broad contrast to divine comprehensive knowledge.
Believers' apprehension of the Hour is joined with recognizing its truth.
The nearby question about earth-born gods contributes to the monotheistic argument without clarifying the focus.
The visible expanse before and behind people is a created sign, not the knowledge relation in the focus.
God's approved religion, worship without association, and movement from fear to security illuminate faithful service under His authority.
The immediate principle that God is not questioned while they are questioned sharpens the asymmetry behind dependent intercession.
Each soul knowing what it brought supplies an accountability counterpart to the focus's complete divine knowledge.
Mixed belief and association contrast with the servants' unqualified submission, but only indirectly.
The local warning that apparent duration does not secure victory gives a distant consequence context.
Messengers arriving from before and behind make the call to exclusive worship comprehensive, though differently from the focus.
Its account of harmful teaching and permission does not materially clarify the focus's authorized intercession.
Repudiates any attempt to inform God of religion because His knowledge encompasses heavens and earth.
A promise of a knowledgeable son does not explain the focus.
Links God's approval, reciprocal approval, and fear of the Lord in a concise reward setting.
The immediate demand for proof against other gods and charge of ignorance frames the focus's exclusive divine authority.
The bodily phrase before their hands and feet has a different function from the focus's before-and-behind formula.
A bare statement of fear supplies too little context to clarify the focus.
The immediate universal message of exclusive worship anchors the servants' obedience and rejection of divine rivals.
Before and behind refer to historical exemplarity rather than the focus's comprehensive knowing.
Their choosing to remain behind and resulting ignorance do not materially develop the focus.
The surah's closing appeal for judgment by truth places contested claims under God's final decision.
Revelation sent with divine knowledge and angelic witness offers only a broad knowledge parallel.
Redirects fear from hostile people to God, clarifying the proper object of faithful fear.
The absence of a protector against punishment gives a distant consequence context for dependent intercession.
God knows the unseen of heavens and earth and sees what people do, broadening the focus's knowledge claim.
The oath by twilight does not materially clarify the focus.
The immediate correction calls the angels honored servants, preparing their obedient, non-independent role in the focus.
Deferring disputed duration to the Lord's greater knowledge is a limited, practical knowledge parallel.
God possesses what is before, behind, and between, and does not forget, strongly expanding the focus's scope formula.
The immediate next ayah gives punishment for any servant claiming divinity besides God, ruling out independent status.
God's hearing and knowledge support recourse to Him, but not the focus's intercessory limitation.
The warning says those gathered to their Lord have no protector or intercessor apart from Him, urging reverence.
The sudden inescapable event adds an accountability backdrop but not the focus's relation of service.
A terse future knowing formula is too general to clarify the focus.
Denies that conjecture can replace truth-bearing knowledge, contrasting with the certainty of divine knowledge.
The arriving soul with driver and witness offers a distant judgment setting rather than a direct link.
A terse future knowing formula is redundant and too general here.
God's knowledge traces movement into and out of earth and between heaven and earth, exemplifying comprehensive scope.
The nearby just scales and sufficient reckoning show the accountable outcome under the One who knows.
What lies before refers to prior revelation confirmed by Gabriel, not the focus's knowledge formula.
Those above fear their Lord and do what they are commanded, closely matching the servants' reverent obedience.
Punishment for setting another god alongside God only generally reinforces exclusive authority.
The repeated future knowing formula remains too general to add beyond the earlier duplicate.
Barriers before and behind depict a contrary loss of sight, contrasting with the unbounded divine knowledge of the focus.
Divine knowledge and wisdom in granting favor is a broad, secondary parallel.
Teaching scripture and wisdom to Jesus does not materially clarify the focus.
Guardians before and behind act by God's command, illustrating a bounded protective role rather than independent agency.
Future satisfaction may echo approval linguistically but gives no usable account of intercession or fear.
Behind refers to opponents affected by a military deterrent, unrelated to the focus's relation.
Those left behind are later companions, not the focus's before-and-behind scope.
Past peoples' rejection and fulfilled warning offer only a general judgment background.
God's hearing and knowledge in provision are too general to develop the focus.
Pregnancy, birth, and lifespan all occur with divine knowledge, illustrating its detailed reach.
God's singular deityhood across heaven and earth with wisdom and knowledge is a broad sovereignty parallel.
Seeking help through patience and prayer is burdensome except for the humble, adding a practical posture akin to reverence.
The local idolaters acknowledge their idols cannot speak, a later illustration of contradicted false claims.
Differing messengers and later conflict do not materially clarify the focus's limitation on angelic intercession.
God's hearing and knowledge authorize seeking refuge, but the setting is temptation rather than intercession.
A prophet's reforming purpose and reliance on God do not materially explain the focus.
God's completed truthful and just word, with hearing and knowledge, is a broad sovereignty parallel.
What was done after Moses does not use behind in the focus's sense.
God alone holds dominion, grants protection, and cannot be protected against, grounding why all mediation is dependent.
Explicitly makes intercession contingent on God's permission, directly paralleling the focus's denial of independent mediation.
Creatures in the heavens and earth, including angels, prostrate without pride, clarifying the servants' humble status.
No one possesses intercession with the Merciful except one who has taken a covenant, closely delimiting access to mediation.
Denies every independent share, aid, and intercessory power besides God, supplying the sovereignty premise for the focus's restriction.
Assigns all intercession to God alone, making the focus's permitted intercession a dependent, not autonomous, act.
The angels bearing the Throne seek forgiveness for believers, a concrete intercessory action embedded in praise and submission.
On the Day of Approach, no intimate friend or obeyed intercessor is available to wrongdoers, showing the boundary of mediation in judgment.
Angels glorify their Lord and seek forgiveness for those on earth, joining reverent service with dependent intercession.
The angels do not disobey God in what He commands and do what they are commanded, closely explaining the focus's obedient servants.
The intercession of intercessors does not benefit the condemned, marking the negative boundary to the focus's permitted exception.
Spirit and angels stand in ranks and speak only when the Merciful permits and with right speech, combining permission, angelic restraint, and accepted utterance.
Those near the Lord are not too proud to worship Him, glorify Him, and prostrate, closely echoing the surrounding portrait of heavenly servants.
Those invoked besides God themselves seek nearness, hope for mercy, and fear His punishment, reversing claims of independent divine agency.
God alone governs creation and has no protector or intercessor apart from Him, grounding dependence before any permitted intercession.
No purported gods can avert harm or rescue, and their intercession would not avail, contrasting false mediation with the focus's authorized exception.
Honored recording guardians are set over people, extending the focus's surrounding knowledge and accountable service through angelic witness.
Its warning that no intercession will be accepted on the Day establishes the judgment boundary against which the focus's exception matters.
Repeats that no soul can answer for another and no intercession is accepted, reinforcing the non-transferability of judgment apart from divine allowance.
The warned soul has no protector or intercessor besides God, connecting fear of gathering with the limits of mediation.
Those once claimed as intercessors disappear at individual return to God, exposing the failure of asserted independent mediation.
Those awaiting fulfillment ask whether any intercessors remain for them, placing hoped-for mediation within irreversible accountability.
The associates will have no intercessors among their alleged partners, directly negating rival mediating powers.
